sources.note: 'No known L1 speakers. Ethnic population: 35,000 (2001 census)'; 'Language Status 9 (Dormant)'; 'Shifted to Malayalam'; 'Language Development: Grammar' (presumably Thampuran 1979); 'Speak a variety of Malayalam [mal] as L1'. Nothing on stress. (Internet Archive copy.)

sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey only; no wordlist was collected for Mala Arayan (p. 767 of text: 'Wordlists from Mala Vedan, Mala Arayan and Ulladan were not collected'). Sec. 2.4 p. 8: 'Mala Aryan used to speak a distinct dialect of their own which was unintelligible to other Malayalis in the past, but now they have adopted the regional Malayalam dialect of their locality (Menon 1996:198).' Sec. 7.3.1 p. 44: 'the Mala Arayan may already have shifted or be in the process of language shift towards Malayalam.' Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Thurston, Edgar (with K. Rangachari). 1909. Castes and Tribes of Southern India, vol. IV (K to M). Madras: Government Press. Entry 'Mala Arayan', pp. 387-395.
